answer: A single delta checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called an ocean, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 378 aliases thus costs 202 bonds held for 17 days each, plus the grove attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
